title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Apply Law to the Act of Felling Forests or Other Trees Owned by One's Own Unit or by Oneself Outside the Location Specified in a Forest Tree Felling License

articles.content_en:
March 26, 2004
Supreme People's Court
Reply concerning How to Apply the Law to the Acts of Felling Forests or Other Woods Owned by the Unit or the Individual beyond the Area Specified in a Forest Tree Felling Permit
Fa Shi [2004] No. 3
To the Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:
Recently, some courts have reported that it remains unclear as to how to apply the law to the acts of felling forests or other woods owned by the unit or the individual beyond the area specified in a forest tree felling permit. Upon study, the reply is as follows:
Any act of felling forests or other woods owned by the unit or the individual beyond the area specified in a forest tree felling permit in violation of the provisions of the Forest Law shall, except for the felling of scattered woods owned by rural residents on their private plots or in front of or behind their houses, fall under the circumstances specified in subparagraph (1) of paragraph 1 of Article 5 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases of Destroying Forest Resources, i.e., "felling without approval and issuance of a forest tree felling permit by the competent forestry administrative department or other competent departments as provided by law," and if the quantity is relatively large, the offender shall be convicted and punished for the crime of illegal felling of trees in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 2 of Article 345 of the Criminal Law.
This reply.
